users.label: People
users.summary: Accounts that own personal work and sign in to Taskiller.
users.why: Keeps identity and access separate from work and session history.
users.lifecycle: Created at registration; profile changes increase its version. Scheduling deletion disables access immediately; the worker later removes the account.

fields.id: Stable identifier used to refer to this person across requests and related records.
fields.email: Sign-in and recovery address; addresses are unique regardless of letter case.
fields.password_hash: One-way password verifier used to check sign-ins; never the raw password.
fields.suspended_at: UTC time an operator suspended this account; empty when not suspended. Suspension blocks sign-in and refresh and revokes product sessions without stopping running Execution Sessions.
fields.suspension_reason: Operator reason for suspension, retained for account lifecycle management and excluded from general API projections. This is separate from pending deletion.
fields.display_name: Optional name shown in the profile; empty when no name was supplied.
fields.email_verified_at: When ownership of the email address was confirmed; empty before verification.
fields.password_changed_at: When the password was last set, recording the latest credential change.
fields.is_active: Whether the person may use the account; switched off when deletion is scheduled.
fields.version: Revision counter increased on changes, allowing clients to detect stale data and, where required, reject conflicting writes.
fields.created_at: When this person record was first saved.
fields.updated_at: When this person record was last changed.

notes: Account deletion is handled by the worker in an explicit dependency order, rather than automatic Django cascades.

user_preferences.label: Personal preferences
user_preferences.summary: One set of display and focus preferences per person.
user_preferences.why: Lets planning and date-based views respect the person’s settings.
user_preferences.lifecycle: Created with the account; updated independently with its own version; removed during account deletion.

fields.user: The person these preferences belong to; also identifies this single preferences record.
fields.timezone: Named local timezone used to interpret local dates and reporting boundaries.
fields.locale: Preferred language and regional presentation setting.
fields.week_starts_on: Chosen first weekday for weekly views, represented from 0 through 6.
fields.preferred_strategy: Default focus approach: auto, continuous, structured, or flexible.
fields.preferred_work_block_min_seconds: Preferred shortest work block for recommendations; empty means no personal minimum.
fields.preferred_work_block_max_seconds: Preferred longest work block for recommendations; empty means no personal maximum.
fields.show_review_prompt: Whether the interface should offer a review prompt after a session.
fields.version: Revision counter increased on changes, allowing clients to detect stale data and, where required, reject conflicting writes.
fields.created_at: When this preferences record was first saved.
fields.updated_at: When this preferences record was last changed.

notes: Relationships use DO_NOTHING: Django does not automatically delete related records; account cleanup is ordered explicitly by the worker.

auth_sessions.label: Sign-in sessions
auth_sessions.summary: A signed-in device or browser and its refresh-token family.
auth_sessions.why: Allows a device’s access to be revoked without confusing it with a focus session.
auth_sessions.lifecycle: Created on sign-in; refreshed while valid; expires or is revoked on logout, security action, or account deletion.

fields.id: Stable identifier used to refer to this sign-in session across requests and related records.
fields.user: The person signed in through this device or browser.
fields.device_name: Optional device label; empty when the client did not supply one.
fields.created_at: When this sign-in session record was first saved.
fields.last_used_at: Last recorded use of this sign-in session, including successful refresh; may be empty if not recorded.
fields.expires_at: Latest time this sign-in session can remain valid.
fields.revoked_at: When this session was deliberately blocked; empty while it has not been revoked.
fields.revocation_reason: Reason access was blocked, such as logout or refresh-token reuse; empty if none was recorded.

notes: Relationships use DO_NOTHING: Django does not automatically delete related records; account cleanup is ordered explicitly by the worker.

refresh_tokens.label: Refresh tokens
refresh_tokens.summary: Stored verifiers for rotating credentials that renew access.
refresh_tokens.why: Supports renewal and detects reuse of an already rotated credential.
refresh_tokens.lifecycle: Issued with a sign-in session; replaced on refresh; expired tokens are removed by retention and all tokens are removed with the account.

fields.id: Stable identifier used to refer to this refresh token across requests and related records.
fields.session: The sign-in session this credential renews.
fields.token_hash: Secret-keyed fingerprint used to match a presented refresh token; not the usable token itself.
fields.created_at: When this refresh token record was first saved.
fields.expires_at: Time after which this credential cannot renew access.
fields.rotated_at: When this credential was exchanged for a replacement; empty until rotated.
fields.revoked_at: When this credential was explicitly invalidated; empty if not revoked.
fields.replaced_by: The next refresh token issued in this rotation chain; empty before rotation or after the referenced expired token is cleaned up.

notes: Reusing a rotated token can revoke the entire sign-in session.
Cleanup clears replacement links before deleting referenced tokens.
Relationships use DO_NOTHING: Django does not automatically delete related records; account cleanup is ordered explicitly by the worker.

email_verification_tokens.label: Email verification tokens
email_verification_tokens.summary: Single-use credential verifiers that let a person confirm ownership of an email address.
email_verification_tokens.why: Makes emailed account actions expire and prevents reuse.
email_verification_tokens.lifecycle: Issued for the email action; marked consumed when used or invalidated by a successful related action; removed after expiry or account deletion.

fields.id: Stable identifier used to refer to this email verification token across requests and related records.
fields.user: The person allowed to use this account action.
fields.token_hash: Secret-keyed fingerprint checked against the emailed token; not the usable token itself.
fields.created_at: When this email verification token record was first saved.
fields.expires_at: Deadline for using this emailed action.
fields.consumed_at: When this action was used or invalidated; empty while it remains unconsumed.

notes: Relationships use DO_NOTHING: Django does not automatically delete related records; account cleanup is ordered explicitly by the worker.

password_reset_tokens.label: Password reset tokens
password_reset_tokens.summary: Single-use credential verifiers that let a person set a replacement password after recovery.
password_reset_tokens.why: Makes emailed account actions expire and prevents reuse.
password_reset_tokens.lifecycle: Issued for the email action; marked consumed when used or invalidated by a successful related action; removed after expiry or account deletion.

fields.id: Stable identifier used to refer to this password reset token across requests and related records.
fields.user: The person allowed to use this account action.
fields.token_hash: Secret-keyed fingerprint checked against the emailed token; not the usable token itself.
fields.created_at: When this password reset token record was first saved.
fields.expires_at: Deadline for using this emailed action.
fields.consumed_at: When this action was used or invalidated; empty while it remains unconsumed.

notes: Relationships use DO_NOTHING: Django does not automatically delete related records; account cleanup is ordered explicitly by the worker.

idempotency_records.label: Request receipts
idempotency_records.summary: Saved outcomes of requests that clients may safely retry.
idempotency_records.why: Prevents a repeated click or network retry from creating the same result twice.
idempotency_records.lifecycle: Claimed and completed within the operation’s transaction; reused for matching retries until expiry, then reset or removed by retention.

fields.owner_id: Person whose request is being remembered; a plain identifier, not a Django foreign-key relationship.
fields.scope: Operation being protected, so one retry key does not collide with an unrelated action.
fields.idempotency_key: Client-supplied retry key; identifies a receipt together with the person and operation.
fields.request_hash: Fingerprint of the original request contents; rejects the same retry key with different contents.
fields.response_status: Saved HTTP outcome for replay; empty until the operation records its result.
fields.response_body_json: Structured response saved for an identical retry; empty before completion.
fields.resource_id: Identifier of the result when the operation has one; empty for outcomes without a linked resource.
fields.created_at: When this request receipt record was first saved.
fields.expires_at: End of the retry guarantee for this receipt.

notes: The combined key is owner_id, scope, and idempotency_key; pk is a virtual convenience, not a stored column.

work_types.label: Work types
work_types.summary: Built-in and personal categories describing how work feels.
work_types.why: Supplies planning characteristics without making people describe every Chore from scratch.
work_types.lifecycle: Built-in types are seeded and read-only through the API. Personal types can be edited and deleted only when no work item still references them.

fields.id: Stable identifier used to refer to this work type across requests and related records.
fields.owner: Person who owns a custom type; empty for a shared built-in type.
fields.slug: Stable short name, unique without regard to letter case within its personal or shared collection.
fields.display_name: Readable category name shown when choosing a work type.
fields.description: Optional explanation of when to use this category.
fields.cognitive_demand: How much mental concentration this kind of work usually needs.
fields.interruption_sensitivity: How disruptive interruptions usually are for this kind of work.
fields.continuity_need: How much this work benefits from an uninterrupted stretch.
fields.repetitiveness: How repetitive the work usually is.
fields.physicality: How much physical activity the work involves.
fields.learning_mode: How learning is involved, helping choose practice or retrieval segments.
fields.is_system: Whether this is a shared built-in type; built-ins have no owner.
fields.created_at: When this work type record was first saved.
fields.updated_at: When this work type record was last changed.
fields.version: Revision counter increased on changes, allowing clients to detect stale data and, where required, reject conflicting writes.

notes: Even soft-deleted work items still prevent deleting their referenced work type.
Relationships use DO_NOTHING: Django does not automatically delete related records; account cleanup is ordered explicitly by the worker.

work_items.label: Work items
work_items.summary: Projects, Sprints, and Chores in one owned hierarchy.
work_items.why: Connects outcomes and plans to the actual work performed in focus sessions.
work_items.lifecycle: Captured as draft work and moved through ready, in_progress, completed, cancelled, or archived. Ordinary deletion marks deleted_at and preserves the row; account deletion removes it permanently.

fields.id: Stable identifier used to refer to this work item across requests and related records.
fields.owner: Person who owns this work and its hierarchy.
fields.kind: Whether this is a root Project, a Project’s Sprint, or an executable Chore.
fields.parent: Containing Project or Sprint; empty for Projects and inbox Chores. A Sprint must belong to a Project.
fields.work_type: Built-in or personally owned category supplying default work characteristics; empty when no category is selected.
fields.name: Work title shown in lists and planning.
fields.description: Optional details about the intended work or outcome.
fields.status: Current progress state, independent of the soft-deletion marker.
fields.position: Ordering value among siblings, used to preserve the person’s chosen sequence.
fields.priority: Optional priority chosen for this item; empty when no priority has been assigned.
fields.estimated_effort_seconds: Expected amount of work, used by recommendations; empty when not estimated.
fields.planned_start_at: Optional intended start moment, used to compare planned and actual work.
fields.target_start_date: Optional calendar start date for a Project or Sprint, rather than a timed appointment.
fields.target_end_date: Optional calendar end date for a Project or Sprint.
fields.cognitive_demand_override: Item-specific setting for how much mental concentration this kind of work usually needs. Empty means use the work type’s value when available.
fields.interruption_sensitivity_override: Item-specific setting for how disruptive interruptions usually are for this kind of work. Empty means use the work type’s value when available.
fields.continuity_need_override: Item-specific setting for how much this work benefits from an uninterrupted stretch. Empty means use the work type’s value when available.
fields.repetitiveness_override: Item-specific setting for how repetitive the work usually is. Empty means use the work type’s value when available.
fields.physicality_override: Item-specific setting for how much physical activity the work involves. Empty means use the work type’s value when available.
fields.learning_mode_override: Item-specific setting for how learning is involved, helping choose practice or retrieval segments. Empty means use the work type’s value when available.
fields.completed_at: When the item was marked complete; empty when no completion is recorded.
fields.cancelled_at: When the item was cancelled; empty when no cancellation is recorded.
fields.archived_at: When the item was archived; empty when not archived.
fields.deleted_at: When ordinary deletion hid this item; empty for items still available in normal lists.
fields.created_at: When this work item record was first saved.
fields.updated_at: When this work item record was last changed.
fields.version: Revision counter increased on changes, allowing clients to detect stale data and, where required, reject conflicting writes.

notes: Projects are roots; Sprints belong to Projects; Chores can belong to Projects, Sprints, or the inbox.
Database relationship guards reject cross-owner links and invalid hierarchy changes.
The API requires live children to be moved or deleted before their parent can be soft-deleted.
Relationships use DO_NOTHING: Django does not automatically delete related records; account cleanup is ordered explicitly by the worker.

focus_plan_recommendations.label: Focus recommendations
focus_plan_recommendations.summary: Saved planning suggestions with their inputs and reasons.
focus_plan_recommendations.why: Makes a recommendation explainable after preferences, work, or the engine change.
focus_plan_recommendations.lifecycle: Created for an executable Chore or Sprint; saved snapshots are read back rather than regenerated. Removed during account deletion.

fields.id: Stable identifier used to refer to this focus recommendation across requests and related records.
fields.work_item: Owned Chore or Sprint this suggestion was made for.
fields.engine_version: Planning-engine revision that produced the suggestion.
fields.provenance: Whether the suggestion used bootstrap rules, preferences, or personal history.
fields.strategy: Focus approach selected by the engine.
fields.input_snapshot_json: Structured copy of work context, available time, requested strategy, preferences, and any personalization signal at generation time.
fields.plan_snapshot_json: Structured suggested plan, including segment kinds and proposed durations as they were generated.
fields.reasons_json: Structured explanations with reason codes, evidence labels, and readable messages.
fields.created_at: When this focus recommendation record was first saved.

notes: Recommendations preserve what was suggested; they are separate from editable Focus Plans.
Relationships use DO_NOTHING: Django does not automatically delete related records; account cleanup is ordered explicitly by the worker.

focus_plans.label: Focus plans
focus_plans.summary: Named sequences of focus segments, optionally saved as templates.
focus_plans.why: Turns a recommendation or manual choice into a reusable execution plan.
focus_plans.lifecycle: Created manually, from a recommendation, or from a template; edits replace segment definitions and increase the version. Soft-deleted through the API and removed permanently with the account.

fields.id: Stable identifier used to refer to this focus plan across requests and related records.
fields.work_item: Chore or Sprint this plan targets; may be empty for an unbound plan or template.
fields.recommendation: Saved suggestion associated with this plan; empty when no recommendation is linked.
fields.source: How the plan was created: manual, recommendation, or template.
fields.name: Readable plan title.
fields.is_template: Whether the plan is saved for reuse as a template.
fields.deleted_at: When this plan was hidden by ordinary deletion; empty while available.
fields.created_at: When this focus plan record was first saved.
fields.updated_at: When this focus plan record was last changed.
fields.version: Revision counter increased on changes, allowing clients to detect stale data and, where required, reject conflicting writes.

notes: Execution uses a saved copy of the segments, so later plan edits do not rewrite a running or past session.
Relationships use DO_NOTHING: Django does not automatically delete related records; account cleanup is ordered explicitly by the worker.

focus_plan_segments.label: Plan segments
focus_plan_segments.summary: Ordered steps defining work, breaks, and supporting activities.
focus_plan_segments.why: Gives the session a clear sequence and duration guidance.
focus_plan_segments.lifecycle: Created or replaced with the owning plan; copied into a session when execution starts; removed during account deletion.

fields.id: Stable identifier used to refer to this plan segment across requests and related records.
fields.segment_index: Zero-based place in the plan; each place is unique within that plan.
fields.kind: Activity for this step: work, break, long_break, retrieval, review, planning, or transition.
fields.duration_mode: Whether timing is fixed, flexible, or open-ended.
fields.target_seconds: Planned duration in seconds, not actual elapsed work; required for fixed and flexible steps, optional for open steps.
fields.min_seconds: Optional lower duration guide; empty when no minimum is specified.
fields.max_seconds: Optional upper duration guide; empty when no maximum is specified.
fields.linked_work_item: Optional Chore to work on in this step: the target Chore itself or a direct child of the target Sprint. Breaks and transitions cannot link work.
fields.optional: Whether the session may skip this step.
fields.label: Optional short caption for the step; empty when the activity kind is enough.
fields.instructions: Optional guidance for carrying out the step.

notes: Relationships use DO_NOTHING: Django does not automatically delete related records; account cleanup is ordered explicitly by the worker.

execution_sessions.label: Execution sessions
execution_sessions.summary: Actual runs of a Focus Plan against a Chore or Sprint.
execution_sessions.why: Records what was attempted while keeping the original plan and work context stable for history and analytics.
execution_sessions.lifecycle: Starts running, can pause and resume, and ends completed or abandoned. Only one running or paused session is allowed per person; account deletion removes its history.

fields.id: Stable identifier used to refer to this execution session across requests and related records.
fields.work_item: Owned Chore or Sprint being executed; Projects must resolve to executable work first.
fields.focus_plan: Plan used to start the run; live edits do not replace the saved session plan.
fields.recommendation: Associated saved suggestion, if one was used; empty for runs without a recommendation.
fields.state: Whether the run is running, paused, completed, or abandoned.
fields.current_segment_index: Zero-based position in the saved plan; advances after finishing or skipping a step.
fields.current_segment_started_at: Timing anchor for the active step; empty between steps or after ending. Resuming shifts it forward to exclude paused time.
fields.paused_at: When the current pause began; empty while not paused.
fields.ended_at: When the run completed or was abandoned; empty while still open.
fields.plan_snapshot_json: Structured copy of segment order, duration choices, links, and instructions captured at start; preserves the plan actually executed.
fields.recommendation_snapshot_json: Structured copy of the linked recommendation and its reasoning at start; empty when no recommendation was used.
fields.work_context_snapshot_json: Structured start-time context for the target and linked Chores, including ancestry, work type, estimate, and planned start, so later edits do not change historical attribution.
fields.created_at: When this execution session record was first saved.
fields.updated_at: When this execution session record was last changed.
fields.version: Revision counter increased on changes, allowing clients to detect stale data and, where required, reject conflicting writes.

notes: Server timestamps govern transitions; the client clock does not control elapsed-time history.
Snapshots are structured application records, not the portable import/export document format.
Relationships use DO_NOTHING: Django does not automatically delete related records; account cleanup is ordered explicitly by the worker.

session_events.label: Session events
session_events.summary: Append-only records of accepted session actions.
session_events.why: Explains how a session reached its current state and lets retries return the original result.
session_events.lifecycle: Added as the session starts and actions are accepted; never edited. Only account deletion may remove them using the database deletion flag.

fields.id: Stable identifier used to refer to this session event across requests and related records.
fields.session: Execution session in which the action occurred.
fields.owner: Person who owns the session; must match the session owner.
fields.type: Action recorded, such as pause, resume, segment completion, or session abandonment.
fields.occurred_at: Authoritative server time of the action, used for ordered history and timing.
fields.client_occurred_at: Optional time reported by the client for context; does not replace server timing.
fields.segment_index: Step this action refers to; empty for actions that do not identify a step.
fields.idempotency_key: Retry key unique within this session, preventing the action from being applied twice.
fields.request_hash: Fingerprint of the action request; detects a retry key reused with different contents.
fields.payload_json: Structured action details, such as a work item to complete; not a standalone portable export.
fields.result_session_snapshot_json: Session response saved immediately after the action, so a retry returns its original outcome even after later actions.
fields.created_at: When this session event record was first saved.

notes: Migration 0004 rejects every event update and rejects deletion unless taskiller.account_deletion is on for the transaction.
Relationships use DO_NOTHING: Django does not automatically delete related records; account cleanup is ordered explicitly by the worker.

session_reviews.label: Session reviews
session_reviews.summary: Optional personal reflection after a completed or abandoned session.
session_reviews.why: Provides explicit feedback for reflection and history-informed recommendations.
session_reviews.lifecycle: Saved only after the session ends; one review per session can be revised, increasing its version; removed during account deletion.

fields.session: Completed or abandoned session being reviewed; also identifies its single review.
fields.owner: Person writing the review; must own the session.
fields.focus_score: Optional self-rating of concentration; empty if not answered.
fields.fatigue_score: Optional self-rating of tiredness; empty if not answered.
fields.difficulty_score: Optional self-rating of how hard the session felt; empty if not answered.
fields.satisfaction_score: Optional self-rating of satisfaction with the session; empty if not answered.
fields.created_at: When this session review record was first saved.
fields.updated_at: When this session review record was last changed.
fields.version: Revision counter increased on changes, allowing clients to detect stale data and, where required, reject conflicting writes.

notes: Relationships use DO_NOTHING: Django does not automatically delete related records; account cleanup is ordered explicitly by the worker.

data_export_requests.label: Data exports
data_export_requests.summary: Background requests for a downloadable personal-data archive.
data_export_requests.why: Lets a person retrieve account and activity records without blocking the request while an archive is built.
data_export_requests.lifecycle: Queued, then processing, then ready or failed. Ready downloads expire; retention clears expired archive bytes and size while keeping request metadata. Account deletion removes the record.

fields.id: Stable identifier used to refer to this data export request across requests and related records.
fields.user: Person whose data is included in the archive.
fields.status: Progress of archive preparation: queued, processing, ready, or failed.
fields.created_at: When this data export request record was first saved.
fields.started_at: When the worker began preparation; empty before processing starts.
fields.completed_at: When archive generation successfully finished; empty before successful completion.
fields.expires_at: When the archive stops being downloadable; set after generation, empty before readiness.
fields.archive_bytes: Gzip-compressed JSON archive held for download; empty before generation or after retention removes it.
fields.archive_sha256: Fingerprint of the compressed archive for integrity checking; empty before generation.
fields.archive_size_bytes: Download size of the compressed archive; empty before generation or after expiry cleanup.
fields.failure_code: Safe explanation code if generation fails permanently; empty when no failure is recorded.

notes: The worker produces taskiller-data-export-v1, a privacy archive; this is distinct from the portable import/export format.
Password hashes, authentication tokens, rate-limit buckets, and internal outbox jobs are excluded.
Relationships use DO_NOTHING: Django does not automatically delete related records; account cleanup is ordered explicitly by the worker.

account_deletion_requests.label: Account deletions
account_deletion_requests.summary: Scheduled deletion requests that survive removal of the account.
account_deletion_requests.why: Tracks the grace period and confirms cleanup without requiring the person’s account to remain.
account_deletion_requests.lifecycle: Scheduling disables the account and revokes sign-in sessions immediately. After execute_after, the worker removes dependent records and the person; completed tombstones are later removed by retention.

fields.id: Stable identifier used to refer to this account deletion request across requests and related records.
fields.user_id: Identifier of the person to delete; deliberately not a foreign key so this completion record can survive deletion of the users row.
fields.status: Deletion progress: scheduled, processing, completed, or failed.
fields.execute_after: Earliest scheduled cleanup time, after the configured grace period.
fields.started_at: When worker cleanup began; empty before processing.
fields.completed_at: When permanent cleanup finished; empty until completion.
fields.failure_code: Safe failure code if cleanup exhausts its retries; empty when no failure is recorded.

notes: DO_NOTHING relationships require the worker to delete dependent rows explicitly, including children before parents.
The worker enables taskiller.account_deletion only within its deletion transaction so guarded session events can be removed.

outbox_jobs.label: Background jobs
outbox_jobs.summary: Durable queued work for email, exports, account deletion, and retention.
outbox_jobs.why: Allows requests to commit intended background work and lets workers recover from interruptions.
outbox_jobs.lifecycle: Queued until available, claimed as running under a lease, then succeeded; failures retry with backoff until dead. Expired leases are recovered; terminal history is retained for a configured period.

fields.id: Stable identifier used to refer to this background job across requests and related records.
fields.job_type: Handler to run: auth_email, data_export, account_delete, or retention.
fields.payload_json: Structured handler inputs, such as a request identifier; email jobs may contain sensitive delivery inputs and should not be exposed as guide examples.
fields.status: Queue state: queued, running, succeeded, or dead after retry exhaustion.
fields.available_at: Earliest time a queued job may be claimed; also carries delayed deletion and retry scheduling.
fields.locked_at: When the current claim began; empty when no worker holds it.
fields.locked_by: Random claim token identifying the current lease, not the worker hostname; empty when unclaimed.
fields.lease_expires_at: Deadline for the claim; empty when unclaimed. Expiry allows recovery and prevents a stale claim from acknowledging completion.
fields.attempts: Number of claims already made, increased each time a worker takes the job.
fields.max_attempts: Claim limit before another failure makes the job dead.
fields.last_error: Last failure’s exception class name, deliberately excluding provider messages that may contain credentials or links; empty before failure or after success.
fields.created_at: When this background job record was first saved.
fields.updated_at: When this background job record was last changed.
fields.completed_at: When the job succeeded or became dead; empty while queued or running.

notes: The worker commits database effects and successful acknowledgement together.
Retry failures clear the claim and defer available_at; exhausted export and deletion jobs also mark their request failed.

rate_limit_buckets.label: Request limits
rate_limit_buckets.summary: Shared counters that limit repeated sensitive requests.
rate_limit_buckets.why: Keeps throttling consistent across API processes without storing raw request subjects.
rate_limit_buckets.lifecycle: Requests increment a counter in a locked row; a new time window resets it. Retention deletes inactive buckets.

fields.scope: Sensitive operation being limited, giving each kind of request its own allowance.
fields.subject_hash: Secret-keyed fingerprint of the limiting subject, which can combine client address and account context; not the raw address or email.
fields.window_started_at: Start of the active counting window.
fields.count: Attempts counted in this window, including attempts above the allowance.
fields.updated_at: Last counted attempt, used to remove inactive buckets.

notes: The combined key is scope and subject_hash; virtual pk has no stored column.

security_events.label: Security events
security_events.summary: Append-only audit records of security-related activity.
security_events.why: Supports investigation without making audit history depend on an account’s continued existence.
security_events.lifecycle: Recorded when security actions occur; never updated. Retention can delete old entries under a dedicated database flag; account deletion does not delete these rows.

fields.id: Stable identifier used to refer to this security event across requests and related records.
fields.user_id: Optional identifier of the person involved; deliberately not a foreign key, so events can exist without a known person and survive account deletion.
fields.event_type: Security action or outcome being recorded.
fields.subject_hash: Optional secret-keyed fingerprint of the client address, allowing related activity to be compared without storing the raw address.
fields.user_agent: Optional client browser or application description, limited to 300 characters; empty when absent.
fields.metadata_json: Structured contextual details supplied by the security action; an empty object means no extra details were provided.
fields.created_at: When this security event record was first saved.

notes: Migration 0005 rejects updates and allows deletion only when taskiller.retention is on for the transaction.
